title: Homepage
findings: Hierarchy
The hero, collections, category rail and filters precede the desktop inventory; the grid heading was around y=842 at a 720px viewport.
Visual weight
Repeated blue frames, raised pills and strong actions make navigation compete with products.
Mobile
Mobile gets products into the first screen. Preserve that advantage while reducing the competing header and dock controls.
fix: Start with search, one category system and the product grid. Define a coherent image, title, price and action hierarchy before extending the design.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Top discounts
findings: Naming
The badge says STEEPEST PRICE DROPS while the explanation says the ranking uses listed discount from MRP. Those are different claims.
Controls
Pink active styling and emoji discount tiers introduce a separate visual language from Discover.
Mobile
The introduction and wrapped filter panel consume much of the screen before products begin.
fix: Name the ranking by its actual basis. Use the shared category/filter pattern and move secondary explanations behind a concise disclosure.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Worth score ranking
findings: Meaning
Algorithmic value leaderboard, God Tier and Mathematical ROI Ranking give a simple heuristic a more authoritative tone than the explanation supports.
Hierarchy
The scoring explanation and tier controls take priority over the products.
Mobile
Stacked score pills form a tall navigation block; the number needs an understandable reason next to each deal.
fix: Use a plain-language ranking name, expose score inputs and limitations, and explain the reason for a score at the item level.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Saved deals — empty
findings: Repetition
The page title, saved badge and empty-state title all repeat the same state.
Content
The local-device storage explanation is valuable but competes with introductory copy.
Action
Browse Latest Deals is relatively quiet inside a large decorative panel.
fix: Use a compact empty state with one clear browse action and a short local-storage explanation.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Saved deals — populated
findings: Layout
A single saved item sits under a full-width search toolbar, creating a sparse inventory layout.
Action weight
Clear All appears beside Find More Deals in the introductory region.
Purpose
This screen repeats discovery cards rather than emphasizing shortlist decisions.
fix: Prioritize revisiting, comparing and removing shortlisted items. Keep destructive bulk controls secondary.
scope: One real offer was saved, opened in Saved, then unsaved to restore the audit session. Desktop state verified.

title: Search results workspace
findings: Layers
Search header, workspace tabs, cross-store banner, source tabs and sorting sit above results.
Naming
Discover/Saved appears again inside the workspace, alongside the app navigation.
Evidence

The count moved from 0 to 80 directory results during the earbuds query. The later mobile capture showed Offer Preview fallbacks. This needs a relevance, provenance and image-loading follow-up; the capture alone does not establish the cause.
fix: Make the query and results dominant. Show directory and external-source status with explicit loading, empty and error states. Check relevance and duplicate counting separately.
scope: Actual earbuds query. Initial desktop and later mobile states captured; search quality and completion were not exhaustively verified.

title: Global search palette
findings: Mixed tasks
One field searches products and utilities, while result rows, merchant filters, trending chips and All 12 Engines share the panel.
Density
Long product titles, discount badges and View labels crowd the compact rows.
Consistency
Rows use a different merchant/discount treatment from the storefront cards.
fix: Separate product results from tool commands and reuse compact product identity rules. Retain keyboard navigation as a useful pattern.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: External store discovery radar
findings: Heading
Google Shopping & Pan-India Radar is a long implementation-oriented title.
Mobile
Title, status, description and close control take a large area above the search input.
States
The reviewed state showed scanning and zero store filters alongside Merchant Checkout Verified. Do not let a persistent positive label imply verification of results that have not loaded.
fix: Use a shopper-facing title, compact query controls and evidence labels tied to actual results. Keep loading state distinct from an empty result.
scope: Live mobile loading state inspected. No successful merchant quote was established.

title: Filter and sort sheet
findings: Strength
The mobile sheet has visible labels and a clear Show results action.
Consistency
Its native selects and broad button contrast are calmer than the multi-pill filters elsewhere.
Opportunity
Selected filters should be visible in the feed after the sheet closes.
fix: Use this simpler interaction as the basis for a shared filtering pattern. Verify applied filters, reset and result counts during implementation.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Product details and price history
findings: Claims
Directory offer, Verified Flipkart, savings vs MRP and DealFlow Verified Price History appear in different parts of the same detail view. Explain exactly what each label verifies.
Priority
The photo, full merchant title, discount and large history panel compete. The desktop footer offers merchant, Scan Stores, Copy Link and expiry actions.
Mobile
The history panel consumes much of the first screen. Product specifications and the next buying decision need a clearer order.
fix: Build an offer summary, then dated price evidence and specifications. Give the merchant action clear priority; put occasional utilities behind secondary controls.
scope: Real Aqua Frisch product opened from the feed. Loaded desktop history showed six recorded checks; no merchant purchase or external-price verification performed.

title: Deal comparison
findings: Mobile
The wide table shows one product column and requires horizontal movement to reach the other.
Hierarchy
Large row labels and a tall heading reduce the visible comparison area.
Source
The source-provided demo compares shoes with a watch, which is unsuitable as evidence of a useful product comparison.
fix: Use a mobile comparison designed around a small shortlist. Keep product identity visible while reading differences; support unlike products without inventing meaningful spec comparisons.
scope: Built-in ?modal=compare fixture. Layout-only review; broken demo images are not treated as a production catalog defect.

title: Specification comparison
findings: Mobile
Wide comparison columns and oversized product headers leave the second item outside the initial view.
Navigation
Offer prices opens a different comparison surface, adding a second layout to learn.
Evidence
Best Price and worth-score rows need clear scope when specifications or scores are not supplied.
fix: Combine price and specifications into one comparison model, with a mobile-friendly way to inspect differences and explicit missing-data states.
scope: Opened from the built-in comparison fixture. Layout and labeling reviewed; live specification completeness not tested.

title: Product price lookup
findings: Layout
A short form sits inside a centered dialog with substantial surrounding empty space.
Naming
Analyzer and Watches introduce another vocabulary beside Price Radar, tracking and alerts.
Input
The URL field relies on placeholder copy to explain supported inputs.
fix: Use a visible Product link label, concise source guidance and a shared price-history entry pattern. Distinguish inspection from saving a target.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Saved price goals
findings: Naming
Watches, saved price goals, alerts and tracked scrapers are competing terms.
Empty state
Add New Link and the explanatory empty-state text point back to Analyzer without making that relationship obvious.
Device scope
The screen says targets are saved on this device; keep this distinct from delivered notifications.
fix: Choose one name for saved targets. Clearly distinguish local goals from active server alerts and offer one direct add-product action.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Price alert registration
findings: Structure
Preset discount targets are useful but the alert title, product panel and channel controls make a long form.
Setup
Telegram instructions are split into short fragments and links below the username field.
Outcome
Arm Price Drop Alert uses a different term from the profile tracker and saved goals.
fix: Use consistent Create price alert wording, explain channel setup in sequence and distinguish submission, active monitoring and delivery confirmation.
scope: Built-in ?modal=alert fixture. Form presentation reviewed; no alert or message was submitted.

title: Profile and product tracking
findings: Overload
Guest identity, four metrics, sign-in, a monitoring form and a how-it-works panel precede account settings.
Vocabulary
Saved Loot, tracked scrapers, Radar and monitors describe related shopper tasks with different terms.
State clarity
Guest view shows Email Live while the preferences section says email notifications require sign-in. Clarify configured versus active status.
fix: Separate account settings from price tracking. Show actionable guest guidance, plain-language targets and honest monitoring status.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Account preferences
findings: Placement
Theme and sound settings are far down the tracking-heavy profile page.
State
Email notifications appear as an enabled toggle beside Requires email sign in; this needs an explicit inactive/needs-setup state.
Consistency
Theme selection appears here and in the global header, with different presentations.
fix: Group account, notifications and appearance clearly. Reuse one appearance control and show prerequisites directly.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: About IndiaDealHunts
findings: Space
Breadcrumb, badge, headline and paragraph consume a large introductory area.
Tiles
Multi-store, When available, On-device and 100% Free are displayed as four KPI-like tiles even though they are different kinds of facts.
Copy
The paragraph claims genuine price drops while other screens carefully distinguish MRP comparisons from observed history.
fix: Use a concise product explanation, clear source limitations and concrete examples of how the product helps a shopper. Replace filler metric tiles with useful content.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: How deals are verified
findings: Title
The title implies a verification process; the introduction describes evidence shoppers can assess.
Reading
Numbered steps are each framed as large cards with extra system labels such as Link Layer and Price Audit.
Mobile
Nested padding creates a long reading experience for short instructions.
fix: State what the service checks, what it does not check and what shoppers must confirm. Use a compact evidence guide with an actual example.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Verification guide dialog
findings: Duplication
The same topic exists as a full page and a five-stage modal.
Navigation
Stage pills, a process strip and footer actions compete with the actual explanation.
Mobile
Source labels, available evidence, what to check and limits are broken into multiple panels.
fix: Use one canonical guide. If a quick explanation is needed, keep it genuinely short and link to the detailed guide.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Wall of Happiness
findings: Empty state
The first capture showed ₹0, zero reports and zero names inside a large metrics panel. Treat these as observed state, not a permanent claim about community activity.
Meaning
Not measured is useful honesty but should not occupy a KPI tile.
Tone
Brag Your Deal Loot does not match the calmer directory language elsewhere.
fix: Lead with actual shopper stories when available. Otherwise use a concise invitation and explain reported versus independently verified outcomes.
scope: Live visual review; initial or default state.

title: Contact and support
findings: Strength
Visible labels, subject selection and a clear message field provide a sound basic form.
Spacing
The shared header, ticker and introductory spacing delay the form on desktop; the narrow mobile form becomes a long page.
Task
Expired deals, partnerships and feature suggestions have different information needs.
fix: Use task-based subjects with relevant helper text and consistent form spacing. Keep the submission outcome visible and explain where responses arrive.
scope: Form inspected without entering personal data or sending a message.

title: Submit a deal
findings: Effort
The form requests product URL, store, price, MRP, notes and email in one long step.
Hierarchy
Store and both price fields have similar weight, while the source link should establish the item first.
Mobile
The vertical form is long; later inputs and the submission action sit below the first screen.
fix: Start with the product link and progressively reveal useful optional fields. Preserve the statement that submission does not guarantee publication.
scope: Form presentation reviewed. No deal submitted.

title: Privacy policy
findings: Strength
A restrained reading surface with section headings is calmer than the rest of the app.
Navigation
A centered modal is the only surface inspected; independent linking, printing and history behavior need checking.
Consistency
The legal dialog uses another header/footer pattern rather than a shared reading layout.
fix: Keep readable line lengths and headings. Provide stable links to policies and a consistent reading surface.
scope: Presentation review only; no legal adequacy assessment.

title: GST input tax credit
findings: Tool-specific hierarchy
Long title, preset prices, tax-rate controls and a highlighted economic-cost result create several levels of framing.
Shared navigation
Search, category tabs, horizontal tool chips, a warning banner and an active-engine footer surround the tool.
Mobile
Shared chrome and the long tool heading consume much of the viewport before useful results. Design for one primary calculation task at a time.
fix: Shorten the title and group price, rate and confirmed eligibility before the result. Keep assumptions adjacent to outputs. Replace Engines, Sentinel and Shield terminology with shopper-facing task names.
scope: Opened live on desktop and mobile with default/example inputs. Visual structure reviewed; arithmetic, current rates, legal/tax rules and financial suitability were not validated. Some captures include entry-transition opacity; no contrast conclusion is drawn from those frames.
